changes.current_line: Billing that helps you grow revenue.
changes.change: For buyers replacing a homegrown billing system, especially product leaders: 'stop it being a tax on the roadmap'. Pricing changes, trials and proration in a few clicks, so a pricing change takes minutes instead of a quarter. Lead the demo with a live price change.
changes.why: The VP of Product rejected the revenue framing ('we're not trying to grow revenue with billing') and named the real problem as 'a tax on the roadmap', and the demo landed when he saw a price change as 'a quarter of roadmap in five minutes'.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: When a champion asks for something for finance, offer a payback model built on the prospect's own inputs, 'a number that's ours', as a one-page summary the champion can take to the CFO. Use the independent study as supporting context for that model, not as the proof on its own.
changes.why: The general ROI deck with the study was sent, but the champion said plainly 'I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours', and his questions had already shifted to things for finance.

changes.change: Add a cost-of-standing-still proof point for finance buyers with a homegrown billing system: what it costs them today in engineering time per pricing change, billing errors, and subscriptions that lapse when a card fails and nobody chases it. Pair the lapse figure with M10 smart retries. Frame it as the case that moves the project from 'nice to have' to funded.
changes.why: The missing piece was 'Their own' number for 'what the homegrown system costs them', the inputs (a quarter per pricing change, lapsed subscriptions from failed cards) were raised but 'We never added it up', and finance treated the project as a 'nice to have' under the rule 'if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded'.

changes.change: Add a migration proof point for billing replacements: a reference customer who moved existing subscriptions without asking their customers for card details again, and did it in stages, available for a peer call. Use it alongside the migration doc, not in place of a peer call.
changes.why: The champion's migration worry was moving subscriptions without re-collecting card details and doing it in stages, and although we had a doc, 'He wanted to talk to someone who'd done it'.
